segments.text: This might be one of the most important videos in this classroom because these are the mistakes I see beginners make all the time.
First, don't assume cheap means bad or expensive means good.
A vendor charging three or four times more doesn't automatically mean the product is three or four times better.
Sometimes you're paying for branding, advertising, packaging or convenience.
Look at the evidence.
Second, don't blindly trust a COA just because you see a PDF saying 99% purity.
Actually verify it.
Check that the compound, batch number, test date and sample information match what the vendor is selling.
Then check which laboratory performed the test.
If the report has a verification number, QR code or report ID, use the laboratory's own website to confirm it whenever possible.
That's also why we built the COA results library classroom so members can review testing documentation we've collected in one place.
Third, don't rely only on reviews posted on a vendor's own website.
Look for independent discussions and patterns over time and don't let a flash sale or only 30 minutes left message rush you into sending money before doing your research.
If you're sending crypto, double check the wallet address before you send anything.
Crypto transactions are generally irreversible, so one wrong character can mean that money is gone.
Also, do not respond to random DMS from people claiming to be a vendor and trying to sell you peptides.
Verify vendor contact information through the official information listed inside the community before communicating or sending payment.
Remember, gray market transactions can have limited consumer protection and something labeled research use only has not automatically been evaluated or approved for human use.
Once you unlock the trusted vendor classroom through community engagement, you'll be able to compare vendor information, pricing and available COAs.
Use Peps by Dave to research smarter, ask better questions and become more informed, not less cautious.
And as always, nothing here is medical advice.
